# Gotchas

Non-obvious traps. Atomic; append new ones.

## hardware (3)

- [[g29-pedal-axes-rest-inverted]] — Two of the G29's pedal axes rest at full scale, so a game auto-binding them reads the pedals as permanently floored ⚠️
- [[keep-g29-selector-on-ps4]] — Leave the G29's console selector on PS4 — it reports 046d:c24f and force feedback works there; advice to switch to PS3 is wrong for this setup
- [[lg4ff-reports-must-be-16-bytes]] — Logitech FFB commands are 7 bytes but must be sent padded to the interface's report length, or the USB endpoint STALLs

## macos (3)

- [[ghub-macos-does-nothing-for-wheels]] — Logitech G HUB on macOS is a firmware updater for the G29 — its HID driver extension only ever loads for two mice
- [[hid-values-need-polling-not-callbacks]] — IOHID input-value callbacks only fire on change, so a stationary wheel reports nothing and a naive read returns "no data
- [[macos-forcefeedback-rejects-g29]] — Apple's ForceFeedback.framework refuses the G29 — it is not PID-class hardware, so every standard FFB API returns nothing

## wine (5)

- [[lfs-performance-dxvk-and-quality]] — LFS stutters on Wine's builtin D3D11 renderer — DXVK plus trimmed quality took it from ~39-58 fps to a steady 100 ⚠️
- [[sdl-wheel-type-changes-axis-usages]] — Enabling Wine's SDL backend makes it emit a wheel descriptor with Simulation Controls axes, and older sims cannot bind those pedals at all ⚠️
- [[sdl2-shim-is-global-to-whisky]] — install-shim.sh patches Whisky's shared Wine library, so it affects every bottle on the machine, not just the sim-racing one ⚠️
- [[wine-macos-has-no-ffb-path]] — Wine on macOS gives games a wheel with working axes and no force feedback — the failure is at capability detection, not at effect playback ⚠️
- [[wine-winhttp-wpad-stalls-steam]] — Steam in the bottle fails with "needs to be online to update" because Wine's WinHTTP runs WPAD proxy detection across all 26 network adapters ⚠️
